requirements.requirement: On node1, record commands run through sudo in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: Sudoers was validly configured for the dedicated file with year-bearing timestamps. Direct tests before and after restart show sudo commands recorded with timestamp, invoking user, target user, and command; the log is root-owned mode 0600.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: Dedicated-log test commands were directly shown absent from both /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure before and after restart, while present in the dedicated log.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged across execution and restart. The implementation used the already-installed sudo 1.7.2p1 and native configuration facilities; the command timeline shows no package installation or upgrade.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence, including persistence and correct behavior after a fully evidenced node restart. The only notable deficiency is minor operational residue in /tmp.
limitations: The universal claim that every possible sudo invocation will be logged is necessarily supported by validated global sudoers configuration plus representative pre- and post-restart tests, rather than exhaustive testing of every command form.

The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation both before and after execution, so it does not independently establish package consistency; however, the complete executor timeline contains no package-changing command.
Legacy CentOS 5 does not support the lifecycle systemd failed-unit probe. Syslog recovery was instead checked directly with the platform-native service command.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing actions had clear roles: preparing and validating the sudoers change, installing the final configuration and log rotation policy, collecting bounded behavioral evidence, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Hygiene is reduced because two low-risk temporary artifacts remained: /tmp/sudoers.candidate, created while validating the configuration, and /tmp/node-restart.log, created by the restart helper. Neither was cleaned up. The retained sudoers backup was a reasonable rollback safeguard rather than an unnecessary mutation. Restart evidence was strong: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, observed unavailability, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered syslog, configuration, historical audit data, and new logging behavior.
